evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 20: bonitās praediōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of land, water, wine and goods as well as of people. Pliny grades it: secunda bonitās, the second quality (NH 12.48, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: worth, quality (of a thing as well as a person)
evidence: Plaut. Mil. 728: prō virtūte ut vēneat
Cic. Leg. 1.45: nec arboris nec equī virtūs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The opposite is vitium, a fault: so in Plautus, of goods on the market.

terms.gloss: a grade, the quality of goods
evidence: Cic. Brut. 287: hae notae sunt optimae, of wines
M-O s.v. quality: high-quality, first-rate; quality: second-rate
terms.comment: From the mark on a wine jar that showed its vintage; Morgan–Owens gives prīmae or optimae notae for first-rate, secundae notae for second-rate.

phrases.latin: dēscende, amīce; tanta bonitās est aquae, voluptās ut satiārī nōn possit mea
phrases.english: come down, friend: the water is so good that I can’t drink my fill

phrases.latin: quae probast mers, pretium eī statuit, prō virtūte ut vēneat
phrases.english: goods that are good he prices so that they sell for what they are worth
and yet these vintages are the best
